title: Hotspot-aware KV slab rehoming and micro-defrag policy for GPU memory smoothing
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Problem: Long-lived KV caches on multi-tenant GPU nodes develop hot/cold skew and micro-fragmentation that increases peak memory tail and causes unnecessary eviction storms during continuous batching. Goal: introduce a hotspot-aware micro-rehoming layer plus a low-latency micro-defragmenter that rebinds small 'hot regions' and enables safe micro-shrink of sparse slabs without global compaction pauses. This work targets reduced 95th/99th percentile memory usage, lower eviction churn during steady-state continuous batching, and improved predictability for Dedicated capacity SLOs.
design_summary: We propose a two-stage approach: 1) Lease-based region rehoming: assign short-lived leases (50-200ms) for hot micro-regions based on access frequency and GPU thread-local heat maps. Leases allow lightweight pointer indirection so hot KV entries can be rebound onto denser micro-slabs co-located with active batches. 2) Background micro-defrag: a low-impact scanner that merges under-utilized fragments inside a slab when utilization < 40% and fragment size distribution indicates >3 gaps. Combining lease windows with conservative prefetch and move-aside ensures no synchronous stalls during serving. Policy is tenant-aware: avoid cross-tenant rebinding that would break isolation unless tenant-level opt-in is set.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Trade-offs: indirection adds one pointer hop for rebounded keys and slightly increases per-entry metadata. Micro-defrag moves small amounts of memory at a time to avoid stalls but may cause transient write amplification. Risks: incorrect heuristics could cause oscillation (hot-to-cold thrash) or increase GPU memcpy traffic under high batch-concurrency. Mitigations: exponential backoff on rehoming for recently-moved regions, per-region rate limits, and telemetry-driven thresholds. Rollback path: ability to disable rebinding at runtime via feature flag and revert to current slabbing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 95th percentile GPU resident memory reduced by >=6% on internal multi-tenant benchmark with mixed short/long contexts; 2) Eviction-related tail latency events reduced by >=25% during continuous-batching 8k qps workload; 3) No increase in median inference latency >2ms; 4) Feature gated with runtime flags and automated rollout to 10%, 50%, 100% with canary checks.
implementation_notes: Components: a small indirection table per-GPU, region lease manager in the runtime, micro-defrag worker with GPU-to-GPU DMA-friendly move paths, and new telemetry counters for rebinding, moves/sec, and memcpy bandwidth. Use cudaMemcpyAsync streams with priority lanes and cooperatively yield to inference streams. Avoid CPU-side copy for large moves; prefer device-local rebinds when possible. We will reuse and extend existing eviction telemetry (ENG-74211 internal) and add new Grafana panels for move traffic and lease churn.
testing_plan: Unit tests for lease lifecycle, property-based tests for rebinding correctness, integration tests exercising continuous batching with synthetic hotspots, and load tests on a 4x A100 staging cluster. Canary rollout with synthetic traffic that replicates customer mix. Performance harness: reuse the 'kbatch-perf' suite and add 'hotspot-sim' scenarios. Run memory-stress job overnight to catch fragmentation edge-cases.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind runtime config; 2) Launch in staging with 5% traffic for 48h; 3) Gradual increase to 25% with telemetry SLO gates (mem 95th, eviction rate); 4) Full rollout and monitor for 72h. If memcpy bandwidth exceeds threshold, automatically revert to previous slab assignment for affected GPUs.
metrics_and_dashboards: New metrics: kv_rebinds_total, kv_moves_bytes, kv_move_errors, kv_lease_renewals, kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_eviction_churn_rate. Dashboards: 'KV Micro-Rehoming' and 'KV Move Traffic' with alerts when moves_bytes/sec > 80% of allowed DMA budget or fragmentation_ratio worsens by >10% post-deploy.
